stdout_text:
Looking at the evidence, I'll evaluate each column.

Key observation: `resolution_hours` should equal `closed_at - opened_at`, but the samples show `closed_at == sys_updated_on` and produce values that don't align with any visible span, plus many negative values — a strong sign of fabrication/unsound computation. `assigned_to_experience` and `category_incident_count` have no source basis in the table (no experience or historical count field) and show suspiciously uniform ramp distributions (0,1,2,3...) suggesting synthetic index generation.

```json
{
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "resolution_hours",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.95,
      "source_groundedness": 0.15,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Directly the dependent variable for the query (resolution time), so highly useful in principle. But values are unsound: many negative hours and figures not reconcilable with the timestamps shown (closed_at equals sys_updated_on, opened_at not reflected). The produced numbers appear miscomputed/invented rather than a valid closed-minus-opened span."
    },
    {
      "name": "priority_numeric",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.8,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "A numeric encoding of the existing priority column gives a clean axis to group/model resolution time against. Largely redundant with the original priority but adds modeling leverage; values are a sound reading of the source."
    },
    {
      "name": "category_type",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Rolls category into higher-level buckets (Infrastructure/Software/Other), a reasonable grouping axis for comparing resolution times. Mappings shown (database, VPN, intranet -> Infrastructure; software update -> Software) are sound categorisations of the source text."
    },
    {
      "name": "is_critical",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.45,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "A binary flag derived from priority (=1 for priority 1). Grounded and consistent (88 criticals match 88 priority-1 rows), but largely a restatement of priority_numeric, giving limited new analytical leverage."
    },
    {
      "name": "assigned_to_experience",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
      "source_groundedness": 0.1,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Agent experience would be a strong explanatory axis for why some agents are slower — highly relevant. But the table contains no experience/tenure information; the near-uniform 0..N ramp distribution and constant 0/1 values on samples indicate a fabricated or index-based synthetic value not derivable from the source."
    },
    {
      "name": "category_incident_count",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.15,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Category workload/volume could plausibly relate to resolution time, so conceptually useful. However the smooth 0,1,2,3... ramp and per-row values (all 0 on Infrastructure samples) do not correspond to any aggregable count grounded in the table; appears to be an invented/index-like value."
    }
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.72,
  "source_groundedness": 0.42,
  "rationale": "The added columns target the right constructs for the query (resolution duration, priority/criticality, category, agent experience, category volume). However groundedness is the major weakness: the core resolution_hours is miscomputed with impossible negative values, and assigned_to_experience and category_incident_count assert quantities with no supporting field in the source, showing telltale synthetic ramp distributions. priority_numeric, category_type, and is_critical are well grounded; is_critical is somewhat redundant with priority."
}
```
